transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Tran (Redwood CSM), John Miller (Quantaco ML Eng), Sarah Lee (Quantaco CTO), Carlos Rivera (Infra), Maya P. (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary: quick review of last week's run, cost-per-token numbers looked promising with caching, some latency regressions at p95 with larger batch sizes, plan to run longer benchmarks and share raw csvs.

00:00 Alex Reed: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call, and we'll get into the numbers - hope that time still works
00:08 John Miller: yep all good, thanks Alex
00:12 Priya Shah: hi team, Priya from Redwood, I'll walk through the benchmark table we ran overnight
00:18 Sarah Lee: hey Priya
00:22 Carlos Rivera: morning folks
00:30 Priya Shah: ok so high level, we ran your sample workload on our hosted cluster and then on a dedicated pool with the quantized 4-bit runtime you asked about, we measured tokens per second and the aggregated cost per million tokens. note: some transcript things will say K V cash instead of KV cache, just ignore that
00:48 John Miller: ha yeah i noticed the term earlier in the doc, it's KV cache for us
00:52 Priya Shah: right, quick disclaimer - we had prefix cache enabled for the hosted run but for the dedicated run we did both on and off to show delta. batch sizes we tried were 1, 4 and 8. sequence length distribution was the corpora you sent: median 80 tokens, p95 420 tokens.
01:18 Priya Shah: so headline numbers, hosted (with prefix cache): tokens/sec ~1200 at batch 4, cost around $1.8 per 1M tokens using on-demand infra assumptions; dedicated (reserved pool, similar util) tokens/sec ~2100 at batch 4, cost ~1.1 per 1M tokens after amortized reserved discount. these are rough, see csv attached in the drive link we shared.
01:45 John Miller: those dedicated numbers look great on paper. question on latency: p50 is fine but p95 got worse when batch=8 on dedicated during peaks
01:58 Priya Shah: yeah that's the tradeoff - batching improves throughput and reduces cost per token, but if you push batch size too high you see queueing latency which shows up in p95. we saw median latency 120ms on dedicated batch=4 and p95 around 740ms when batch=8 during the spike window.
02:18 Sarah Lee: do you have the exact traffic shape where you saw the regression? queued requests or longer sequences?
02:24 Priya Shah: mostly queued requests - the traffic spike aligned with a subset of large sequence requests (p95 sequences) and our batcher held for more requests to fill batch=8, so a high-latency tail formed.
02:36 Carlos Rivera: can you tweak the batching policy? e.g., max wait 20ms or dynamic batch by sequence length?
02:44 Priya Shah: yes, we can do dynamic batching by seq len and max wait windows; Redwood's runtime supports sequence-aware batching to avoid piling short and long seqs. we recommended max wait of 10-20ms for your SLA of ~500ms p95 but we can tune.
02:58 John Miller: ok makes sense. what's the cost delta if we go with max wait 10ms vs 50ms?
03:05 Priya Shah: rough ballpark from runs: at 10ms wait the tokens/sec was ~1900 (batch effective ~3.5) and cost ~1.2 per 1M tokens; at 50ms wait tokens/sec ~2200 and cost ~1.0 per 1M tokens. so about 15-20% better cost for longer wait but at p95 you'd see more latency.
03:28 Alex Reed: also remember prefix cache impacts this a lot for your workload - you had ~35% prefix repetition in the corpora, enabling prefix/KV cache reduced tokens generated by roughly 25% effective cost in hosted run.
03:42 Maya P.: that 35% number - is that stable across datasets? in prod we expect some variation
03:48 Priya Shah: it's sample dependent, we recommend running a 24-72h replay to get stable numbers; early runs can under/overstate caching savings.
03:58 John Miller: did you measure cache hit vs miss effects on latency?
04:02 Priya Shah: yes, cache hits are faster since KV lookups are cheap relative to full decode, p50 for hits was ~90ms vs ~130ms for misses in our hosted runs. however misses are where sequence length matters. there's also CPU memory pressure on the host if cache grows a lot, so we cap cache size and evict LRU.
04:22 Sarah Lee: for compliance we need to ensure cache entries can be encrypted and audited - is that supported?
04:28 Alex Reed: yes, Redwood Private/Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS and audit logs for cache operations; we'll include the security doc in the follow-up.
04:36 Carlos Rivera: good. one more infra question - for on-prem we have fixed GPU count, can Redwood runtime still do batching and caching effectively?
04:44 Priya Shah: yes, runtime is hardware-aware and will pick kernel variants; the main lever is batch size and number of worker replicas. on smaller GPU pools you typically run smaller batch sizes but increase concurrency to keep latency targets.
04:58 John Miller: switching gears to tokens/sec/$ calculation - can you share formula you used? we want reproducibility
05:05 Priya Shah: sure - tokens/sec/$ we present as (tokens_per_second) / (dollars_per_second). dollars_per_second is derived from hourly infra price divided by 3600 and any amortized reserved discount applied. for clarity we also give cost per 1M tokens = (1,000,000 / tokens_per_second) * dollars_per_second. we'll include the spreadsheet formula in the csv.
05:30 John Miller: great. I noticed an odd discrepancy in the hosted run when prefix cache was enabled we saw a slightly higher CPU load and occasional GC spikes
05:38 Priya Shah: that sounds like our cache write path - on high write churn we saw memory allocs. we can move to a write-behind or batched write design for heavy write workloads in the POC; it's enabled as an opt-in.
05:50 Sarah Lee: what's the expected improvement if write-behind is enabled?
05:55 Priya Shah: we measured about 10-15% lower CPU and noticeably smoother tail latencies in a synthetic high-churn test. not a silver bullet but helps.
06:04 Alex Reed: who owns enabling that in POC?
06:08 Carlos Rivera: we can enable on our side if Redwood exposes the flag, otherwise Redwood can flip in the hosted environment for the test window
06:16 Priya Shah: we can expose it as a config flag for the POC; Priya (laugh) will flip it and rerun.
06:23 John Miller: (laughs) great.
06:26 Priya Shah: also worth noting we saw some transcription mismatch in the automated logs - i mean not transcription, but label mix ups like Speaker 1. ignore that in the doc.
06:34 Alex Reed: ok next topic - model variants and fallback. we had the model A (full precision) and A-quantized 4-bit variant; fallback to a cheaper model during load is possible. any concerns?
06:48 Sarah Lee: if fallback changes output quality we need to detect regressions. what's Redwood's approach?
06:52 Priya Shah: Redwood Optimize can run evals on a prompt set and raise regression alerts; for the pilot we recommend a small eval set to monitor quality delta before you enable automatic fallback.
07:04 John Miller: perfect. can we threshold fallback on both latency and regen quality - like only fallback if latency > 1.2s and quality metric delta < 0.02?
07:13 Priya Shah: yes, policies can be composite. we'll help write the policy for the pilot.
07:18 Alex Reed: quick check - does Quantaco expect to go Dedicated after pilot or stay Hosted?
07:23 Sarah Lee: tentative toward Dedicated if we can hit cost numbers and maintain <600ms p95; otherwise prefer Hosted for ops reasons.
07:32 Alex Reed: understood. dedicated usually wins on unit economics if you have steady volume. we modeled a 3-month commit discount in the quote draft.
07:41 John Miller: about the batch tradeoffs - you mentioned dynamic batching by seq len; can you share pseudo-configs?
07:46 Priya Shah: yes - sample rule: for seq_len <128 allow batch up to 8, for 128-512 allow up to 4, over 512 batch up to 2; max wait 10ms for short sequences and 30ms for mid sequences. i'll paste these heuristics in the follow-up.
08:03 Carlos Rivera: will we be able to simulate our QPS shape? we have diurnal spikes, bursts of 2x baseline for 5-10 minutes
08:10 Priya Shah: we can replay traffic in our test harness; please share the real traffic CSV and we'll run a 24h replay with the chosen batching config.
08:18 John Miller: ok will do.
08:20 Maya Tran: quick note from CSM, we'll schedule a 24h replay run for next Tuesday and attach the raw logs to the drive.
08:28 Alex Reed: thanks Maya.
08:30 (brief cross talk)
08:40 John Miller: one more thing on cost math - do your cost numbers include storage and networking overhead for cache syncs?
08:46 Priya Shah: good call - our rough numbers included compute only; networking and storage costs for heavy cache writes would be incremental; for hosted we estimate extra $0.05-$0.1 per 1M tokens in heavy-write scenarios, for dedicated it's usually lower since it's internal traffic. we'll add that delta column.
09:06 Sarah Lee: also security - audit logs for cache ops and SSO integration timelines?
09:12 Alex Reed: we can support SAML SSO and we will share SOC2 + ISO docs; audit log retention is configurable, we included a 90-day default in the pilot.
09:22 Carlos Rivera: is there an encryption option for cache at rest?
09:26 Priya Shah: yes, we support KMS integration for Private/Dedicated and envelope encryption for hosted caches; specifics in the security pack we'll attach.
09:34 John Miller: great.
09:36 Priya Shah: circling back to benchmarking plan - we'll run: baseline (no cache), cache-on with write-behind enabled, varying batch sizes 1/4/8 and dynamic batching rules; 24h replay and capture p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, and cost metrics.
09:58 Alex Reed: audience question - what's the most conservative config that meets your p95 target?
10:02 John Miller: probably batch 4 with max wait 10ms and prefix cache on
10:08 Priya Shah: that aligns with our intermediate numbers - cost slightly higher but within your target if cache hit rate stays >30%
10:14 Sarah Lee: ok, also quantify tail risk if cache evictions spike during traffic bursts
10:19 Priya Shah: we can add a stress test scenario to the replay: increase churn and force cache evictions, measure the delta.
10:26 John Miller: perfect.
10:29 Alex Reed: action items recap - Priya to run benchmarks and share csv, Alex to send updated quote, John to share prompts and traffic, Carlos to confirm infra constraints. any additions?
10:41 Sarah Lee: can you also include a simple cost sensitivity chart (cost vs batch size vs cache hit%) in the follow-up?
10:48 Priya Shah: yes we'll include that chart and a short explanation of assumptions.
10:55 John Miller: last question - are there any known instability issues with the 4-bit quantized kernels on longer sequences? we had one run where the model returned early stops
11:03 Priya Shah: rare but there are edge cases; we do kernel-level guards and also suggest running evals for your long-seq prompts. if you see hallucinations or early stops we'll capture and escalate to the infra team.
11:16 Alex Reed: ok we're at 40 minutes, appreciate the deep discussion. we'll aim to run the 24h replay early next week.
11:24 Maya Tran: I'll create the calendar invite for the replay results review and attach the drive links.
11:30 John Miller: thanks everyone, huge progress.
11:35 Alex Reed: thanks all - we'll follow up with csvs, price, and security pack.
11:42 (meeting ends)
